transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-03 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood); Marta Lopez, James O'Neill, Priya Singh (Argosy)

Summary (auto): Quick follow-up after the 10/31 outage - go over RCA, immediate mitigations, confirm rollout and next steps.

[00:00] Alex Chen: ok, hey everybody, thanks for joining uh we'll run 55 minutes ish, uh the goal is to go through the postmortem, confirm mitigations and finalise the rollback/patch schedule
[00:12] Marta Lopez: thanks alex, thanks priya. we just wanna make sure we have a concrete timeline, and that the SLA credits and the dedicated plan are on the table
[00:25] Priya Nair: yeah hi all, quick context recap - the outage started when the kv cache eviction path hit a bad codepath during a spike, that caused repeated model reloads and the routing fallback flooded the hosted pool, pushing us over throttles
[00:41] James O'Neill: just to be clear, we saw 5xxs then long tails, our traces show lots of stall on the kv cash (sic) layer and some ordering issues in the kernel selector, we captured trace ids and histograms
[01:05] Priya Singh: security check - we didn't see data exfil or any customer PII exposure, logs are encrypted, KMS keys were fine, but audit logs were delayed which made the triage harder
[01:30] Alex Chen: thanks, so root cause in short: regression in an optimization that touches the kv cache + poor fallback throttling policy under simultaneous canary rollout and a traffic spike. the patch is to revert that optimization and add stricter semaphore limits on fallback routing
[01:52] Marta Lopez: and the immediate mitigation we asked for last week - the emergency rollback - that reduced errors but we want the patch plan so we don't repeat the revert cycle
[02:08] Priya Nair: agreed, plan is: (1) hotfix to remove problematic path and add stronger guardrails (2) update routing policy defaults to limit burst fallout (3) add prefix-aware cache instrumentation and alerting
[02:30] Alex Chen: timeline? when can priya's team deliver the hotfix and tests?
[02:36] Priya Nair: we have a patch branch, running stress tests now, expect canary by 2026-11-06 and full rollout 2026-11-09 if tests pass. I'll share the CI logs and the test harness link
[02:55] James O'Neill: can you run the same load pattern we hit - our load had a high number of short sessions, lots of KV cold prefixes, that's important for reproducing the failure
[03:08] Priya Nair: yes we'll reproduce with the same short-session trace. Priya (redwood) to share trace generator and config within 24h
[03:18] Marta Lopez: on the dedicated capacity topic, we need predictable throughput, can you send pricing and a guaranteed latency SLA?
[03:27] Alex Chen: yes i'll send a dedicated proposal with reserve sizes and SLA credits, also include an option for burst capacity we discussed - will email by 2026-11-09
[03:40] Priya Singh: on compliance, we need the audit log retention and proof of KMS rotation, also SSO/SAML changes for the runbook access - will need docs
[03:52] Alex Chen: we'll attach SOC2 scope, KMS rotation docs and the updated runbook access controls in the postmortem package
[04:05] James O'Neill: are there any plan changes to the alerting? our team missed the threshold because the alert aggregated at 5m granularity
[04:18] Priya Nair: yes we'll add per-route tail-latency alerts at 1m and a saturation alert for fallback routing. also add a synthetic probe that simulates short-session prefix churn
[04:35] Marta Lopez: can you also add a playbook step for immediate escalation to Redwood SEs? during the outage it took too long to get a triage owner assigned
[04:46] Alex Chen: we'll formalize escalation steps and contact matrix - SE oncall details and a rapid postmortem template
[05:00] (brief crosstalk)
[05:10] Priya Nair: ok walking through the postmortem doc linked in the chat: section 1 incident timeline, section 2 technical RCA, section 3 mitigations, section 4 long term reliability improvements
[05:26] Alex Chen: help me with the long term items - caching strategy, kernel selection validation and dedicated routing path for critical tenants
[05:36] Priya Nair: long term we propose: prefix-aware persistent cache buckets for high-churn prefixes, an offline kernel-validation job before canary, and a per-tenant dedicated routing option that pins to reserved capacity to avoid noisy neighbor effects
[05:58] James O'Neill: sounds good. we want to add a SLA clause for sustained p95 and p99 bounds if we go dedicated, and a rollback triggers list for any canary that crosses tail-latency delta of >20%
[06:19] Alex Chen: noted. i'll include rollback triggers in the rollout plan. about the runbook, who owns the immediate triage step?
[06:25] Marta Lopez: Argosy SRE will do initial triage, but Redwood SE must be on the initial 15 min call once we hit defined error thresholds
[06:33] Priya Nair: we'll map alert thresholds to an escalation policy. also add a runbook appendix for trace collection with exact CLI commands to get the kv snapshot and kernel debug logs
[06:50] (silence while someone checks chat link)
[07:05] Marta Lopez: quick question - will the fix require downtime or rolling restarts?
[07:12] Priya Nair: rolling restarts only, no full downtime. we plan to throttle canary traffic to avoid the cascade. we will pause automated autoscaling during the rollout window to keep predictable behavior
[07:28] James O'Neill: ok that helps. one more ask - can we get 30 days of increased logging retention for audit/troubleshooting?
[07:36] Alex Chen: yes can add as a temporary retention bump, we'll include cost impact in the proposal
[07:44] Priya Singh: and on the security front, we'll need to audit who accessed certain debug keys during the incident, can you share the provisional access log?
[07:53] Priya Nair: yes we have access logs, we'll redacted PII and share via secure link in the postmortem packet
[08:05] Alex Chen: ok let's summarize next steps: redwood to share full incident doc + raw logs by 11/05, priya to run targeted reproducer and share results by 11/05, patch canary 11/06, full rollout 11/09, pricing and dedicated SLA proposal 11/09
[08:28] Marta Lopez: and argosy to confirm acceptance criteria for reliability improvements by 11/10 - we'll review the runbook and escalation steps then
[08:40] Alex Chen: perfect, action items in the chat. any other questions?
[08:46] (no response)
[08:50] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing and with the runbook session - meeting adjourned

References shared in chat: incident_postmortem.pdf (link), stress-harness.zip (link), dedicated-pricing-sheet.xlsx (link).

Notes on transcription: some names may be misattributed, occasional ASR errors (kv cash, etc.).
